messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into German, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE German line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.
Nachdem ich mich ein wenig ausgeruht hatte mein müder Körper, ging ich wieder den Weg entlang der verlassenen Böschung, so dass der feste Fuß immer der tiefere war.

Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

### Summary of Issues - **WRONG:** *fermo* (“firm”) is not rendered in the German clause; the translation loses the attribute of the foot. - **UNNECESSARY (target‑side addition):** the German sentence adds the adverb **wieder** (“again”) in line 29 (“ging ich **wieder** …”), which is not present in the source. - **GRAMMAR:** The first German line **„Nachdem ich mich ein wenig ausgeruht hatte mein müder Körper,“** is syntactically incomplete in German; a verb linking “mein müder Körper” to the preceding clause is missing (e.g., “…, war mein müder Körper …”). This makes the clause ungrammatical as a whole, though each individual word is correctly translated.
All other source words are covered with appropriate German equivalents and correct grammatical agreement.
